subject: Data sanitization logbook, geofence segmentation and attestation follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Tang <sara.tang@brightmart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightmart.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify: logbook, onshore backups, and proof of destruction

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has a few follow-ups before we can sign the DPA appendix: they want a clear description of how Redwood documents deletion of customer data from (a) active inference stores, (b) periodic onshore backup snapshots, and (c) any ephemeral caches used for batching. Specifically:

- What record do you keep when an erasure request is processed (log fields, retention of that log)?
- For backups that are stored onshore (US region) but are also part of a multi-geo replication chain, how do you prove the backup slice was sanitized for BrightMart data?
- Is there a downloadable attestation or runbook we can present to auditors showing the steps and retention windows?

Can you provide an example attestation and an outline of the runbook/procedure (including roles, run-commands if applicable, and expected evidence artifacts)? We want to avoid lengthy redline cycles in the DPA.

Appreciate a concise runbook and any templates you can share.

Best,
Sara
Sara Tang
Contracts Lead, BrightMart

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Tang <sara.tang@brightmart.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 20:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: logbook, onshore backups, and proof of destruction

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Dumping a short runbook and an attestation template below and attaching a PDF runbook + attestation doc (see attachments). High level answers first, then the artifacts: 

High level:
- Erasure logging: every erase request generates an immutable event in our audit log with fields: request_id, customer_id, object_type (prompt, response, cache_key, snapshot_id), erasure_scope (active|backup|cache), operator_id (system|human:email), start_timestamp, completion_timestamp, affected_shards, verification_hash (SHA256 over wiped sector map), and evidence_links. Audit logs are retained for 2 years by default (configurable in Enterprise plans).
- Backups & multi-geo: Onshore backup slices are tagged with region metadata and a backup manifest. When we perform customer-scoped sanitization, the backup manifest is updated with a sanitization entry that includes the slice_id, sanitized_ranges, action (zero-fill|trim|skip), operator, and attestation_token which is a signed statement from our KMS stating the sanitized ranges. For replicated backups we propagate the sanitization marker; if a downstream replica is outside the requested geofence we trigger a repair job to remove any residual BrightMart blobs and re-issue the attestation.
- Ephemeral caches: caches used for batching are TTL-based and also subject to synchronous zeroing upon a legal erasure request; wiped cache sectors are recorded in the same audit events as above.

Attached artifacts (see attachments):
- redwood-data-sanitization-runbook-v1.pdf: step-by-step ops runbook for data erasure flows, expected logs, sample commands, and verification checklists.
- onshore-wipe-attestation-template.docx: customer-facing attestation template we can populate after a targeted sanitization.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We (Redwood) fill the attestation template for BrightMart test account and send it to Legal within 48 business hours once you confirm scope.
2) If Legal wants a short, signed technical attestation (HSM-signed token) we can add the attestation_token and an accompanying verification endpoint in the console.
3) For DPA language, suggest a clause: "Sanitization of customer data from backup slices will be recorded and evidence provided within X business days; for replicated slices outside the original geofence Redwood will remediate and provide proof within Y business days." Happy to propose exact X/Y values after you confirm acceptable windows.

Looping Lauren (Product) and Marissa (Compliance) for operational details and the attestation scope.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sara Tang <sara.tang@brightmart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightmart.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 01:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: logbook, onshore backups, and proof of destruction

Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying follow-ups from Legal: 

- For the audit log retention, can you confirm whether the 2-year default is configurable per-customer (yes/no) and whether logs are exportable in raw format for our auditors?
- For the attestation_token flow: is the token revocable and does it include a signed timestamp and KMS signature we can verify independently? We want to tie the token to an HSM-signed statement if possible.
- For replicated backups: if a replica exists in an EU region and BrightMart requests a US-only residency, can Redwood guarantee removal from that EU replica (or provide an exception process)? What is the typical remediation timeline you expect for cross-region repairs?

Legal also asked for one real example of a sanitized backup manifest entry (redacted) to confirm the fields. If you can populate the template and attach a redacted manifest snippet, that will speed review.

Thanks,
Sara

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Tang <sara.tang@brightmart.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: logbook, onshore backups, and proof of destruction

Sara — thanks, happy to provide the artifacts. Summary + attachments and concrete answers below: 

1) Audit log retention: configurable per-customer. Default 2 years; Enterprise customers can request 1/3/5 year retention via the Console or during onboarding. Logs are exportable in CSV/JSON and we can provide an auditor bundle (signed manifest + logs) under an NDA.

2) Attestation token: implemented as an HSM-signed JWT with fields: subject(customer_id), action(sanitization), slice_id, sanitized_ranges, issued_at, issuer(kms@redwood), signature. Tokens are revocable: we maintain a revocation list and publish token status via a verification endpoint. We will include the verification endpoint URL in the attestation when we send it.

3) Cross-region replicas and remediation timeline: we do guarantee removal from replicas under our DPA remediation process. Typical timelines: 
- If replica is in same cloud provider and region-pairing (within US): 3-5 business days.
- Cross-region (e.g., EU replica for a US residency request): 7-14 business days for detection + repair + attestation, depending on data volume.

4) Attached: a redacted manifest snippet and a populated attestation template (both attached). The manifest snippet is sanitized — it includes the slice_id, sanitized_ranges, action, operator_id (system-redacted), and attestation_token_id.

If BrightMart Legal is OK with a 7-14 day remediation SLA on cross-region replicas we'll add specific DPA language: we recommend X=5 business days for same-region backups and Y=14 business days for cross-region replicas. If you need tighter SLAs we can scope reserves or dedicated Dedicated capacity/Private deployment options.

Ben and Marissa — let me know if you want me to send the signed attestation from KMS or if we should wait for Sara to confirm scope first.

—
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Data Controls — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
